dataset_family: Retrospective multi-hospital Taiwanese rsEEG cohort: Yang-Ming Hospital (Taoyuan), Chi-Mei Medical Center (Tainan), Taipei Veterans General Hospital; 205 participants (51 CN, 42 MCI, 112 AD across CDR 1-3) plus a 72-patient MCI longitudinal cohort
method_family: 19-channel eyes-closed rsEEG; Holo-Hilbert spectral analysis (two-layer EMD) amplitude-modulation power features against windowed-FFT and HHT band-power features; LogitBoost feature selection plus seven classifiers (10-fold CV / train-test split); cluster permutation group maps
what_it_shows: A within-study, head-to-head MCI-vs-CN classification of HHSA amplitude-modulation power features against conventional windowed-FFT band-power features (and HHT) using the same seven classifiers. Best HHSA accuracy is 0.81 (GentleBoost) and best FFT accuracy 0.78 (Naive Bayes). Classifier by classifier, HHSA is better for 3 (Bag 0.76 vs 0.68, GentleBoost 0.81 vs 0.73, Tree 0.73 vs 0.68), equal for 2 (LogitBoost 0.76, k-NN 0.70) and worse for 2 (SVM 0.70 vs 0.73, Naive Bayes 0.76 vs 0.78).
why: No. The measure is outside the statement's class. HHSA amplitude-modulation power is a second-order spectral power representation (power of the amplitude envelope at each carrier frequency). It is not a network, connectivity or complexity measure, and the authors themselves equate it with band-limited power (p.14). They also say AM power is only a 'necessary condition' for cross-frequency coupling, which would additionally require identifying the modulation source (p.13). What the study shows is that one spectral decomposition marginally beats another, not that network, connectivity or complexity measures outperform band power. The margin itself is small and mixed (HHSA better for 3 of 7 classifiers, equal for 2, worse for 2). Features were chosen from group-level contrasts ('features extracted from group-level comparison', Table 4 title), and the MCI test set is only 17 (Table 1), so the accuracies are optimistic and unstable. MCI was defined by CDR 0.5 and MMSE >= 25 without biomarkers, and CN are younger (69.6 vs 73.5 years). Independence: no site, cohort or author overlap with P-553, P-501, P-463 or P-480, or with the other candidates. Not in registry_duplicates.json. The block (headed by filename) matches the PDF on title, authors and DOI. Block and registry defect: 'What is the sample size?' and Sample_N_Approx both say 51, but N is 205 cross-sectional (51 CN / 42 MCI / 61 AD1 / 35 AD2 / 16 AD3) plus 72 longitudinal MCI.

quotes.quote: HHSA-based feature extraction outperformed other methods, with the GentleBoost algorithm surpassing other classifiers with a sensitivity of 82%, specificity of 80%, and accuracy of 81% (Table 4 and Supplementary Figure 19).

The AM power shown here is comparable to band-limited power (BLP), which extracts AM power based on FFT band-passed filter followed by the Hilbert transform.
The presence of AM power in the f c is the necessary condition for CFC though CFC requires identifying the modulation source (Juan et al., 2021).
Subsets of 100 features from the tens of thousands of remaining features were applied to the LogitBoost algorithm to select limited (<10) high-ranking important features to avoid overfitting
